from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [

        group_a = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FF5733") for _ in range(10)]).arrange_in_grid(2, 5)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Rule of Summation", [
            "Adding two normal variables is a new normal.",
            "The mean of the sum is the sum of means.",
            "The variance of the sum is the sum of variances.",
            "The combined distribution is a new bell curve.",
            "This rule applies to all independent Gaussian distributions."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_A = "#FF5733"
        COLOR_B = "#3357FF"
        COLOR_SUM = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Adding two normal variables is a new normal.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_SUM)
        formula = MathTex(r"S = X + Y", color=COLOR_SUM)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The mean of the sum is the sum of means.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_SUM)
        group_a = VGroup(*[Dot(color=COLOR_A).move_to(self.grid["D2"] + np.random.normal(0, 0.1, 3)) for _ in range(10)])
        self.play(FadeIn(group_a))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The variance of the sum is the sum of variances.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_SUM)
        group_b = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.1, color=COLOR_B).move_to(self.grid["D5"] + np.random.normal(0, 0.1, 3)) for _ in range(10)])
        self.play(FadeIn(group_b))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The combined distribution is a new bell curve.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_SUM)
        combined = VGroup(group_a.copy(), group_b.copy())
        self.play(combined.animate.move_to(self.grid["E4"]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This rule applies to all independent Gaussian distributions.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_SUM)
        self.play(FadeOut(formula), FadeOut(combined))
        conclusion = Text("Independent Gaussians Sum!", font_size=24, color=COLOR_SUM)
        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, "C3")
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Two narrow distributions represent specific uncertainties.",
            "Adding them shifts the mean to the right.",
            "The final curve is wider due to added variance.",
            "This visual superposition confirms the rule of summation.",
            "Uncertainty grows as we combine independent processes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Uncertainty Accumulation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid setup
        grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(2):
            for j in range(3):
                dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
                grid.add(dot)
        grid.arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=3, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        
        # Color rows in #FF5733 and columns in #33FF57
        row1 = VGroup(grid[0], grid[1], grid[2])
        row2 = VGroup(grid[3], grid[4], grid[5])
        self.play(row1.animate.set_color("#FF5733"), row2.animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        
        col1 = VGroup(grid[0], grid[3])
        col2 = VGroup(grid[1], grid[4])
        col3 = VGroup(grid[2], grid[5])
        self.play(col1.animate.set_color("#33FF57"), col2.animate.set_color("#33FF57"), col3.animate.set_color("#33FF57"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        # Animate moving a single row to reveal the structure
        self.play(row2.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.5))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FFBD"))
        # Change color of the grid border to #33FFBD
        border = SurroundingRectangle(grid, color="#33FFBD", buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(border))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#33FFBD"))
        # Just emphasis, no complex movement per instructions

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        # Fade out grid and show the multiplication result '6'
        result = Text("6", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(result, 'D4')
        self.play(FadeOut(grid), FadeOut(border), FadeIn(result))
        self.wait(1)

        self.setup_layout("Real-world Application & Summary", [

            "Complex systems become predictable with this arithmetic.",

        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show an icon representing a menu
        menu_icon = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color="#FF5733")

outline.topic: The Additive Property of Normal Distributions: Gaussian + Gaussian = Gaussian
outline.target_audience: University students (Statistics, Engineering, or Data Science)

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 min)
sections.content: Briefly define a Normal Distribution N(μ, σ²) using the Bell Curve visual. Explain that adding two random variables is equivalent to calculating their convolution. Introduce the concept of independent variables.
sections.example: Imagine two independent robots measuring the distance to a wall; each measurement has a 'blur' or error defined by a Bell Curve.

sections.title: The Rule of Summation (1.5 min)
sections.content: State the core theorem: If X ~ N(μ₁, σ₁²) and Y ~ N(μ₂, σ₂²), then X + Y ~ N(μ₁ + μ₂, σ₁² + σ₂²). Use an animation showing two shifting Bell Curves merging into a new, wider Bell Curve.
sections.example: Robot A has error N(0, 1) and Robot B has error N(0, 2). The total combined error of the system is N(0, 1+2) = N(0, 3).

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Why' (1.5 min)
sections.content: Show the graphical superposition. Explain that the mean shifts by the sum of means (linear) and the variance spreads out by the sum of variances (Pythagorean-like addition of uncertainty).
sections.example: Visual overlay: Two narrow spikes merging into one 'fatter' curve, representing how uncertainty accumulates when processes are stacked.

sections.title: Real-world Application & Summary (1 min)
sections.content: Apply the concept to a real scenario. Conclude that for independent Gaussian processes, the total output remains predictable and Gaussian. Emphasize that this simplifies complex systems into basic parameter arithmetic.
sections.example: A package delivery process: Time to sort (N(10, 2)) + Time to drive (N(30, 5)) = Total time N(40, 7). The total distribution is still a smooth, predictable Bell Curve.
